title: Koya Lead Agent
summary: An evidence-grounded lead research and outreach-drafting system that discovers companies, researches public sources, qualifies leads, drafts outreach, and routes uncertain decisions through human review.
problem: Lead research is easy to automate badly. A useful system has to turn a vague objective into explicit qualification criteria, collect trustworthy company evidence, keep long-running research observable, control cost and provider usage, and avoid turning uncertain research into confident outreach claims.
system: The application converts a user objective into an explicit ICP, discovers candidate companies, researches public company websites, records evidence-backed qualification decisions, drafts a three-step email sequence plus a LinkedIn message, and keeps a human reviewer in control of final qualification and copy approval.

engineeringDecisions.title: Separate web and worker processes
engineeringDecisions.detail: Long agent runs execute outside the request lifecycle so the interface stays responsive while work continues durably.

engineeringDecisions.title: Enforce limits outside the model
engineeringDecisions.detail: Candidate, scrape, tool-call, turn, and spend limits are controlled by application code rather than model instructions.

engineeringDecisions.title: Treat research as evidence, not truth
engineeringDecisions.detail: Qualification stores source URLs, confidence, fit reasons, concerns, and review states instead of collapsing incomplete research into a binary answer.

reliability.title: Safe pause, resume, and cancellation
reliability.detail: Control requests are checked at safe execution points and saved state avoids repeating completed research unnecessarily.

reliability.title: Prompt-injection boundary
reliability.detail: Scraped website content is untrusted data and cannot alter objectives, runtime limits, or the available tool surface.

reliability.title: No-send boundary
reliability.detail: The agent has no email, SMTP, LinkedIn sending, or personal-email lookup tool; it stops at reviewed drafts.

reliability.title: Deterministic provider testing
reliability.detail: Recorded provider fixtures keep routine tests repeatable and prevent accidental provider spend.

result: A review-first research system that can carry a lead from objective to evidence-backed qualification and outreach drafts while keeping uncertainty, provider failures, spend, and human approval explicit.

evidence.label: Source repository
evidence.description: Public monorepo with web, worker, core domain rules, database migrations, and test suites.

evidence.label: Automated verification
evidence.description: Repository includes unit, contract, integration, replay, and Playwright end-to-end coverage.

title: RAG Application
summary: A multi-user RAG application with authentication, persistent document storage, vector retrieval, conversation memory, and user isolation across storage, vector, and database layers.
problem: A document-chat demo becomes a real application only when users can authenticate, upload multiple document formats, retain their files, isolate knowledge from other users, preserve conversation context, and manage documents without leaking state between storage layers.
system: A FastAPI backend authenticates users with Google OAuth, stores uploaded documents in Google Cloud Storage, indexes document chunks into user-namespaced Pinecone vectors, persists metadata and conversation state in MongoDB, and streams grounded answers through an Agno RAG agent.

engineeringDecisions.title: Isolate every persistence layer
engineeringDecisions.detail: GCS prefixes, Pinecone namespaces, and MongoDB filters all carry the user identity instead of relying on a single isolation boundary.

engineeringDecisions.title: Persist source files
engineeringDecisions.detail: Uploads are stored in GCS rather than temporary local disk so document management remains durable across server restarts.

engineeringDecisions.title: Keep conversational state
engineeringDecisions.detail: Session history and agent memory are persisted separately from document vectors to support contextual follow-up questions.

reliability.title: Secure session cookies
reliability.detail: Authentication uses server-side session handling with HTTP-only cookies and time-limited serialization.

reliability.title: Coordinated deletion
reliability.detail: Document deletion removes the corresponding file, vector entries, and metadata instead of leaving stale knowledge behind.

reliability.title: Multi-format ingestion
reliability.detail: PDF, DOCX, and TXT inputs flow through the same upload and indexing boundary.

result: A reusable authenticated RAG backend that treats document storage, retrieval, user isolation, memory, and lifecycle operations as first-class product concerns rather than only demonstrating retrieval quality.

evidence.label: Source repository
evidence.description: FastAPI application, storage helpers, agent configuration, and document-processing code.

title: Koya Proposal Studio
summary: An AI-assisted proposal workflow that moves from discovery input to generation, manual editing, immutable version review, independent approval, PDF generation, and controlled delivery.
problem: Generating a proposal is only one step of a real sales workflow. The harder requirement is ensuring the exact content submitted for review stays stable, approval is independent, delivery is controlled, and failures are visible rather than silently corrupting the workflow.
system: Sales users capture discovery context and supporting materials, generate and revise proposal sections, submit an immutable version for an independent approver, generate the approved content as a client-facing PDF, and deliver it through a controlled email boundary with delivery history.

engineeringDecisions.title: Immutable proposal snapshots
engineeringDecisions.detail: Every generation, regeneration, and manual edit creates a new version so reviewed content cannot change underneath an approver.

engineeringDecisions.title: Enforce workflow state in the database
engineeringDecisions.detail: RLS and security-definer RPCs protect submission, approval, and delivery transitions beyond the UI layer.

engineeringDecisions.title: Keep approval independent
engineeringDecisions.detail: The exact submitted version is read-only in approval and self-approval is blocked at the database level.

reliability.title: Recoverable delivery state
reliability.detail: Delivery attempts are logged, including uncertain outcomes where the provider response cannot be safely interpreted as success.

reliability.title: Sandbox-safe email testing
reliability.detail: A provider-boundary redirect supports sandbox delivery without changing the real client email displayed in the application.

reliability.title: Workflow test pack
reliability.detail: Prepared scenarios exercise intake, generation, supporting materials, approval, delivery, and important edge cases.

result: A proposal application where AI generation is embedded inside a controlled business process with traceable versions, independent sign-off, and an explicit delivery boundary.

evidence.label: Source repository
evidence.description: Next.js application, Supabase migrations, generation flow, approval system, and delivery implementation.

evidence.label: Workflow test pack
evidence.description: Prepared end-to-end scenarios for the proposal lifecycle and failure cases.

title: Real-Time Voice AI Agent
summary: A real-time voice-agent integration that combines LiveKit’s low-latency media pipeline with Agno’s tool calling, knowledge, memory, and agent capabilities.
problem: Real-time conversational AI needs more than an LLM response loop: speech detection, transcription, audio streaming, synthesis, tool use, persistent context, and a user-facing meeting surface have to cooperate without turning the conversation into a high-latency request chain.
system: A custom LiveKit Agents integration lets an Agno agent participate in a real-time voice pipeline while retaining Agno’s tools, knowledge, memory, and session identity. A LiveKit Meet interface provides the room experience used to interact with the agent through voice or chat.

engineeringDecisions.title: Bridge agent intelligence into the media runtime
engineeringDecisions.detail: The integration keeps LiveKit responsible for real-time voice infrastructure while Agno supplies agent reasoning and higher-level capabilities.

engineeringDecisions.title: Preserve session identity
engineeringDecisions.detail: Session and user identifiers allow memory and context to persist beyond a single utterance.

engineeringDecisions.title: Treat Meet as the interaction surface
engineeringDecisions.detail: The LiveKit Meet application is presented as the UI/runtime companion to the agent integration rather than as a separate portfolio project.

reliability.title: Streaming response path
reliability.detail: The agent emits responses into the real-time pipeline instead of waiting for a full batch completion before playback.

reliability.title: Explicit provider configuration
reliability.detail: LiveKit, model, and transcription credentials are isolated through environment configuration.

result: A practical real-time agent foundation that joins a proven media transport layer with tool-capable, memory-aware agent behavior.

evidence.label: Agno integration repository
evidence.description: Custom integration between Agno agent capabilities and LiveKit Agents.

evidence.label: Meeting interface repository
evidence.description: LiveKit Meet surface used for real-time interaction with the agent.

title: Koya Content Studio
summary: An evidence-grounded research and content system that takes a request through source review, planning, generation, evaluation, channel adaptation, approval, and an internal publishing queue.
problem: AI content systems can produce polished copy without a trustworthy factual basis. The workflow needed to make source selection and evidence review visible before generation, preserve reviewed versions, and distinguish internal scheduling from external publishing it could not verify.
system: Users can research the web or supply source material, inspect retrieved evidence, resolve source conflicts, approve the source set, generate and evaluate article options, adapt selected content for multiple channels, package exact versions for human approval, and schedule approved outputs in an internal queue.

engineeringDecisions.title: Review sources before writing
engineeringDecisions.detail: The source set becomes an explicit user-reviewed artifact before substantive generation begins.

engineeringDecisions.title: Version evidence and content
engineeringDecisions.detail: Source sets, evaluations, articles, channel outputs, and review packages remain stable after later edits.

engineeringDecisions.title: Separate preparation from publication
engineeringDecisions.detail: The application queues and schedules content internally but does not claim LinkedIn, X, or email publication it cannot verify.

reliability.title: Ground factual generation
reliability.detail: Substantive claims are based on reviewed evidence rather than relying on model memory.

reliability.title: Human package approval
reliability.detail: The exact article and channel versions are assembled into a review package before they become schedulable.

reliability.title: Explicit publishing boundary
reliability.detail: External delivery is intentionally outside the system instead of being simulated or inferred.

result: A content workflow that makes research provenance, source review, content versions, approval, and the limits of automation visible throughout the process.

evidence.label: Source repository
evidence.description: Application source for research, evidence review, content development, approval, and internal scheduling.

evidence.label: Application checks
evidence.description: Repository includes unit/integration tests, Playwright end-to-end tests, lint/type checks, and production build checks.

title: Operations Reporting & Decision Support
summary: A cross-functional operations reporting system that computes deterministic business KPIs, persists data-quality evidence, and layers AI decision support onto authoritative results.
problem: Operational reporting becomes misleading when AI is allowed to invent or recalculate business metrics. The system needed a dependable way to compute KPIs, preserve the exact run, expose data-quality limitations, and still use AI where interpretation is valuable.
system: An n8n automation processes reporting data across Sales, Project Delivery, and People Ops, persists deterministic KPI results and quality issues in Supabase, and a Streamlit dashboard loads the exact run to present authoritative metrics alongside model-generated summaries, risks, and recommended actions.

nodes.label: Supabase
nodes.detail: Runs, metrics, AI insights, quality issues

engineeringDecisions.title: Keep KPI math deterministic
engineeringDecisions.detail: Business metrics are persisted by the automation and treated as authoritative; the dashboard does not silently recalculate them.

engineeringDecisions.title: Use AI for interpretation
engineeringDecisions.detail: Model output adds executive summaries, risks, and recommended actions without replacing the underlying calculations.

engineeringDecisions.title: Expose data quality
engineeringDecisions.detail: Limitations and issue registers are part of the report rather than hidden when source data is incomplete.

reliability.title: Partial-run usefulness
reliability.detail: Deterministic reporting remains available when the AI interpretation step is unavailable.

reliability.title: Exact-run dashboard loading
reliability.detail: The UI loads the report run returned by the workflow instead of showing whatever happens to be most recent.

reliability.title: Manual calculation evidence
reliability.detail: Separate KPI workbooks reproduce Sales, Project Delivery, and People Ops calculations for cross-checking.

result: A reporting system that separates factual operational measurement from probabilistic management interpretation while making data quality and calculation evidence visible.

evidence.label: Dashboard repository
evidence.description: Streamlit command center that triggers the automation and renders persisted report runs.

evidence.label: KPI calculation evidence
evidence.description: Manual calculation workbook verifies the Sales, Project Delivery, and People Ops KPI logic.

title: Intelligent Invoice Processing
summary: An automated invoice-ingestion workflow that extracts structured invoice data from email and documents while explicitly handling duplicates, incomplete fields, non-invoices, unreadable files, and extraction failures.
problem: Invoice automation fails in practice when it assumes every email contains a valid, readable invoice with complete fields. Real inboxes contain duplicates, notices that are not invoices, damaged files, scanned PDFs, and incomplete documents.
system: The workflow screens incoming email, identifies invoice candidates, extracts structured fields from email bodies or PDF attachments, validates required information, builds a deduplication key, stores successful or warning-state records, and sends rejected or failed inputs to an explicit error log.

engineeringDecisions.title: Separate candidate detection from extraction
engineeringDecisions.detail: Irrelevant mail and clear non-invoice notices are filtered before expensive extraction work.

engineeringDecisions.title: Keep warning states
engineeringDecisions.detail: An otherwise useful invoice with a missing field can be stored as processed-with-warnings instead of being treated the same as a corrupted document.

engineeringDecisions.title: Persist a stable dedupe key
engineeringDecisions.detail: Duplicate detection is represented directly in stored workflow data rather than relying on human review.

reliability.title: Duplicate handling
reliability.detail: Repeated invoice inputs are logged as duplicates rather than silently inserted twice.

reliability.title: Unreadable-file handling
reliability.detail: Damaged PDFs and files without usable text layers create explicit extraction failures.

reliability.title: Non-invoice handling
reliability.detail: Payment-method reminders and unrelated newsletters are recorded as non-invoice/not-candidate outcomes.

result: A workflow that demonstrates automation reliability through the unhappy paths as clearly as the successful extraction path, with a usable audit trail for every processed email.

evidence.label: Processed invoice register
evidence.description: Evidence includes successful PDF/body extraction and warning states for incomplete fields.

evidence.label: Failure register
evidence.description: Evidence includes duplicate, non-invoice, irrelevant-email, damaged-PDF, and no-text-layer outcomes.

title: Malaria Detection with CNNs
summary: A two-stage computer-vision application that first validates uploaded blood-cell imagery and then classifies valid cells as malaria-infected or uninfected.
problem: A malaria classifier should not confidently classify arbitrary images that are outside its training domain. The application needed a simple guard before the diagnostic model so obvious non-cell inputs would not be treated as blood-smear predictions.
system: Users upload an image through Streamlit. A first classifier checks whether the input is a valid blood-cell image; accepted images are then resized for a CNN that predicts infected or uninfected and returns a confidence score with analysis time.

engineeringDecisions.title: Add an input-domain gate
engineeringDecisions.detail: A separate cell-image classifier rejects obvious non-cell imagery before malaria inference.

engineeringDecisions.title: Deploy the model as an interactive app
engineeringDecisions.detail: Streamlit turns the trained classifiers into a testable end-user workflow rather than leaving them in a notebook.

reliability.title: Explicit invalid-input path
reliability.detail: Non-cell images produce an error state instead of an infected/uninfected prediction.

reliability.title: Confidence and analysis time
reliability.detail: The interface exposes prediction confidence and processing time alongside the class result.

result: An applied-ML project that demonstrates both model inference and a simple but important guardrail around the model’s intended input domain.

evidence.label: Source repository
evidence.description: Streamlit deployment script and trained model artifacts for validation and malaria classification.
